 This Mfa Is Filed Under Section 173(1) Of Mv Act
Against The Judgment And Award Dated:02.09.2011
Passed In Mvc No.133/2010 On The File Of The Senior
Civil Judge And Additional Mact, Harihar, Partly
Allowing The Claim Petition For Compensation And
Seeking Enhancement Of Compensation.
 This Appeal, Coming On For Orders, This Day, The
Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

1. The claimant, being dissatisfied with the compensation of Rs.1,58,635/- awarded by the Tribunal,
is in appeal.

2. The fact that the accident occurred and the further fact that the offending vehicle was insured is not in dispute.
3.

The Tribunal, on assessment of the evidence, has recorded a finding that the claimant has suffered the following injuries:
"Fracture of both bones of left leg and middle 3rd and also head injury"
4.

The Tribunal has thereafter awarded the following sums as compensation:
Sl. Compensation under Amount No. different Heads in (Rs.)
1 . Pain and sufferings 40,000 2. Loss of future income 49,500
3. Medical expenses 33,135 Ayathkhan vs H. G. Palakshappa on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89516697/
2 4. Loss of income during the laid 6,000 up period 5.
Conveyance, food, nourishment, 10,000 attendant charges 6. Loss of amenities in life 20,000 Total 1,58,635 5.
The Tribunal, on an analysis of the medical evidence, has concluded that the claimant has suffered permanent physical disability to the extent of 8% to the whole body.
6. The Tribunal has determined the monthly income, notionally at Rs.3,600/-.

Since there is no credible documentary evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income, it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority,
which, for the accident of the year, 2009 would be Rs.5,000/-.
7. As the claimant was aged 55 years, a multiplier of '11' would have to be applied.

Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.52,800/- (Rs.5,000 x 12 x 11 x 8%) towards 'loss of future income'.
8.
As a consequence, the amount of Rs.6,000/- awarded by the Tribunal towards 'loss of income during the laid up period' would also stand enhanced to Rs.10,000/-.

9. The sums awarded as medical expenses, pain and suffering, loss of amenities and medical attendant charges and nourishment by the Tribunal are just and proper and do not call for modification and hence confirmed.

10. Consequently the award of the Tribunal is modified and the claimant would be entitled to the following compensation:
 As As  awarded awarded  Sl. Compensation under by the by this  No. different Heads Tribunal Court  (Rs.) (Rs.)
 1. Pain and sufferings 40,000 40,000
2 . Loss of future income 49,500 52,800

3. Medical expenses 33,135 33,135  Loss of income during 6,000 10,000  4.
 the laid up period  Conveyance, food, 10,000 10,000  5. nourishment, attendant  charges Ayathkhan vs H. G. Palakshappa on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89516697/
3  6. Loss of amenities in life 20,000 20,000

11. Thus, the claimant is held entitled to the total compensation of Rs.1,65,935/- as against Rs.1,58,635/-, along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
12. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
13. The claimant would not be entitled for the interest on the compensation for the delayed period of 2160 days in filing the appeal.
14. The disbursement of the compensation amount shall be in terms of the award of the Tribunal.
15. The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
